convoLines.text: "Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"You know what, fair." Ella nods slowly. "I can see how that looked. But here's the thing..." And the thing is mundane, and verifiable, and fine.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
The ease drains out of it, a little.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"I stay where I'm useful. Right now that's here. Cape Town, South Africa is a direction, not a plan. Here is a plan, even if it's a hard one."
"Is that so? Still on whether you're staying."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Life's funny that way."
"Good question." "Cameron owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I hate to ask this, but I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Will you help me?"
"The cut's gone hot and it's spreading — I can feel it moving. Clean it out, wrap it tight, please. Before it turns."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Duel. They just... took Stan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I sharpen sticks down to nothing. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said you're staying — you didn't expect to say it, but you said it. Still true?"
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Stan — Duel, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know where the purslane grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Leo owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"I'm picking up Leo's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Like I said — Still on what's been happening."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally?"
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
Their tone levels out — courteous, careful, further away.
"Still on how this changed you. That matters to me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? ...sorry."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Leo is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I count portions out loud before eating for Leo, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
